label: Fixation is at least i/M when selection does not oppose the mutant
statement_en: In an absorbing chain on 0..M gene copies whose expected copy number never decreases (neutral, or selection for the mutant), a lineage present in i copies is eventually fixed with probability at least i/M. Wright-Fisher sampling with mutant relative fitness 1+s, s >= 0, is such a chain. Hence the expected number of substitutions over T generations is at least mu T (and at most M mu T), whatever M.

hypotheses.name: favored-fixation-lower-bound#assumed-1
hypotheses.statement: The expected count is a DEFINITION (rate x generations, independent fates, Kimura 1968); linkage, interference, changing M, changing s and overlapping generations are excluded by it, not shown absent.

hypotheses.name: favored-fixation-lower-bound#assumed-2
hypotheses.statement: Selection enters only through the sampling probability (1+s) i / (M + s i), constant in time and across sites.

hypotheses.name: favored-fixation-lower-bound#assumed-3
hypotheses.statement: mu, T, M are free parameters; the module measures nothing. Which mutations are favored, how many a trait needs, and in what order, are outside it.

kernelChecked: For any absorbing chain on {0..M} copies with E[X_{t+1} | X_t = i] >= i (stochastic, both ends absorbing, positive one-step escape from every interior state), P(fixed by t) is nondecreasing and bounded, its limit u(i) exists, and u(i) >= i/M (Delphi.FavoredChain.fixationProbability_ge); also u(i) <= 1.
Wright-Fisher sampling with success probability (1+s) i / (M + s i), s >= 0, is such a chain (Delphi.wrightFisherSelection), so a single new mutant fixes with probability at least 1/M.
The defined expected count M mu u T equals mu T for the neutral Wright-Fisher chain, is at least mu T for any favored chain, and is at most M mu T for any u <= 1.
assumed: The expected count is a DEFINITION (rate x generations, independent fates, Kimura 1968); linkage, interference, changing M, changing s and overlapping generations are excluded by it, not shown absent.
Selection enters only through the sampling probability (1+s) i / (M + s i), constant in time and across sites.
mu, T, M are free parameters; the module measures nothing. Which mutations are favored, how many a trait needs, and in what order, are outside it.
